<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via authorization_code (symbol, a field of const object INVALID_GRANT_DESCRIPTION), invalid_grant (literal, a string literal in refuseGrantForBannedUser))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), verifyMcpAccessToken (literal, a string literal in resolveExecutionContext))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx`  _(via invalid_token (literal, a string literal in INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN_WWW_AUTHENTICATE; a string literal in refuseUserInfoForBannedUser))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via authorization_code (symbol, a field of const object INVALID_GRANT_DESCRIPTION))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via resolveExecutionContext (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via invalid_grant (literal, a string literal in refuseGrantForBannedUser))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), authorization_code (symbol, a field of const object INVALID_GRANT_DESCRIPTION))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 49 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce22ba450713376a29c843eff83b8596d41b5500` — the merge of head `6efeaf733aa20c6d2dd5c0a9c5a4abd322e5f200` into base `14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce22ba450713376a29c843eff83b8596d41b5500 && git checkout ce22ba450713376a29c843eff83b8596d41b5500
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12 6efeaf733aa20c6d2dd5c0a9c5a4abd322e5f200 && git checkout -B drift-repro 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12 && git merge --no-ff 6efeaf733aa20c6d2dd5c0a9c5a4abd322e5f200

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `949fd3f1e4bb6c97599741c67440907bc5eb2053`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-error-code.pin.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts, packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/user-ban-write.ts, the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.12` and `better-auth@1.7.12` (admin, device-authorization, one-time-token, jwt plugins), read from the pnpm store. Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; `reviewFace` finds no schema or governed path), so the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces. The changeset itself is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; it is read here only for ②. Full review (no prior at-tier record on this PR). Independence: ④ run by a subagent that did not draft the change; the seat adopts.

### ① Derived judgments

Every path on this head that turns an OAuth credential into a principal, or mints a new token or session for the same user, enumerated from the code and judged against the stated rule ("a ban holds every credential of the user"):

1. **MCP HTTP door, access token** (`resolve-execution-context.ts:191-210`) — COVERED. The ban is read once per verified token, outside the verifier's net, with the shared predicate `isUserBanInForce` (`core/security/user-ban.ts:55`) and the same read shape as the key-admission seam (`core/security/api-key.ts:770-783`): primary key, `USER_BAN_FIELDS`, `limit: 1`, `isSystem`. A banned subject gets exactly the unverified-bearer envelope (`session: 'none'`, guest, no cookie fallback). Correct. The verifier (`auth-manager.ts:4411`) stays local and I/O-free, as its docblock now records. The MCP transport is stateless (`mcp-server-runtime.ts:1965`, `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`) and the dispatcher resolves per request (`http-dispatcher.ts:1112`), so no principal survives across requests. Correct.
2. **MCP door, in-process forward credential** (`resolve-execution-context.ts:182-183`) — COVERED. A forward whose agent acts for a banned user resolves as one that does not redeem; the control pins equality with an unredeemable handle. Correct.
3. **Token endpoint, `refresh_token`** (`oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts:71-77`; wired at `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:696-699`) — COVERED. In the installed provider the one minter every user grant reaches calls `customTokenResponseFields` before the refresh rotation and before any token row or signature; the refresh handler writes nothing before the minter. The refusal is the provider's own `400 invalid_grant` / `invalid refresh token`, pinned against the real provider's answer (class, status, body, cache-control, www-authenticate) and in the dogfood against a misdirected real refresh token. Correct, and "leaves every row as it was" holds on this arm.
4. **Token endpoint, `authorization_code`** — COVERED as defence in depth, but the body overstates it. In the installed provider the code handler consumes the code and requires the code's session to still exist before the minter (and so before this hook) runs. Both ban routes on this head end the user's sessions (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts:181`; the vendor route does the same), so for a ban placed the normal way a pre-ban code is refused by the provider's own session check, with its own `invalid_request` description, and never reaches the hook; the hook's `invalid code` answer is reached only when a session survived the ban. Either way no token is minted — the rule holds — but "`400 invalid_grant` with the provider's own description (`invalid code`)" (PR body, changeset line 8) and "leaves every row as it was" (`oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts:22-27`) describe the uncommon case, and the code is consumed before the refusal on this arm. The real-provider describe pins the refresh arm only (`auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts:423-481`); the code arm is pinned at module level alone.
5. **Token endpoint, extension grants** — COVERED by construction: an extension handler issues only through the provider's bound `issueTokens`, which is the same minter. None is wired on this head, so the claim is correct and currently vacuous.
6. **Token endpoint, `client_credentials`** — OUT BY CONSTRUCTION: no user row; the MCP verifier refuses M2M tokens anyway (`auth-manager.ts:4365-4377`). Body says so. Correct.
7. **Authorize + consent** — OUT BY CONSTRUCTION: needs a live session; the ban routes end sessions and the vendor's `session.create` hook refuses a banned user (the same hook `core/security/user-ban.ts:7-9` names). Correct.
8. **Device-authorization `/device/token`** (opt-in) — OUT BY CONSTRUCTION: mints a session through the internal adapter, so the same `session.create` hook refuses it. Not an oauth-provider grant; not named in the body, harmless.
9. **jwt plugin `/token`, one-time-token verify** — OUT BY CONSTRUCTION: session-bound (the first also mints a token without the MCP audience, which the verifier refuses). Not named; harmless.
10. **stdio MCP, REST, GraphQL** — OUT BY CONSTRUCTION: API key or session only (`mcp/src/plugin.ts:268`, `current-user-endpoints.ts:593-596`); keys are covered on `main` by the predecessor.
11. **Principal-session mint and agent-forward identity view** — already refuse a banned user on `main` (`principal-session-mint.ts:266`, `agent-forward-identity-view.ts:170`). Correct.
12. **The authorization server's own endpoints** (`auth-route-ledger.ts:352,421,424,428`) — NOT NAMED. The body's "A ban holds every credential of the user" and the changeset's "Nothing else narrows" state a scope wider than the doors the diff names; the body has to list exactly which doors the rule holds at, these included or excluded. Detail is in the reviewer's local note, not here.

Fault classification: a thrown ban read is `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('sys_user')` (503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) unless `isMissingTableError(err, 'sys_user')`; a missing table and a missing row both answer "not banned" — byte-for-byte the key-admission seam's posture, pinned (`resolve-execution-context.test.ts:887-909`). Correct. The ban read sits outside the verifier's `try`, so a store fault is never laundered into "did not verify". Correct. The token endpoint adds no read, so no new fault class there. Correct.

APIError code pin (`api-error-code.pin.test.ts:137-145`): the third accepted shape requires a string-literal `error` AND an `error_description` on the same literal; fixtures accept the two compliant spellings and report a bare literal `error`, a non-literal `error`, and a description alone (`[true,true,false,false,false]`, `:261-269`). Narrow enough; both directions pinned. Correct.

Tests are rule tests: the banned answer is asserted `toEqual` a real control on every door (unverified bearer, unredeemable handle, misdirected refresh token, made-up MCP token), with the write-landed-nothing read, cost pin, expiry in both spellings, not-banned/unbanned/no-row/no-table controls, and the timed-ban lapse. Ablation evidence in the body (three ablations at `9032503647`, each red then restored blob-equal) covers both resolver checks and the grant refusal. Accepted.

Accept-set change: the narrowing the changeset declares is exactly what the diff does at the MCP door and on the refresh arm; on the code arm the declared envelope is the uncommon case (item 4). No public export is added or removed; `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` patch, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch — correct: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner, and both lines carry `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` plus `Metadata-protocol: none` and the single ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true` and needs none; `@objectstack/core` is not touched by this diff. Changeset present for every published touched package. One accuracy point folded into ① item 4 (should-fix, not a level question).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay author to name.
- No open card is referenced; the only number in the body is the merged predecessor, with no closing keyword beside it. Correct.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — …` (PR body line 3): still `follow-up owed`, no `#N`, and no such card exists (issue search on the named files and wording returns none). The checklist makes an unfiled follow-up on a `(narrowing)` change a REWORK. The predecessor resolved the same line by editing the two docs pages in-PR (`Skills-docs: updated here`); the pages and the Ban User confirmation (`administrator-guide.mdx:84,184`, `authentication.mdx:1256`, `sys-user.object.ts:210`) each list what a ban refuses and are one clause short. Must-fix: either edit them here, or file the card (rule-level wording only) and write its number into the line.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts:1-3`: no `// test-budget:` header line. The file boots the showcase, runs two DCR-to-token flows and waits a timed ban out, so it is over the 10 s line by construction; its sibling from the same series declares `// test-budget: 20 — spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture: …` (`api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts:2`). Without the declaration the file is its lane's card the day it lands. Must-fix: declare the budget from a measured reading, same class.
- CI at head `949fd3f1e4`: every check-run `success` or `skipped` (the UI jobs skip on the paths filter; Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI all `success`). Not a governed-surface PR; Tier S/H does not apply. The body's full-dogfood red (`package-commit-revert-path-package`, a timeout under load, green alone at the same head) is unrelated to this diff and reported as such.
- `open_questions`: none declared by the dev. Reviewer's questions: see ④.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published behaviour on `main`: it takes nothing from a consumer that the rule does not already take from sessions and API keys; it makes the ban real for two more credential kinds at the doors that resolve them, reads the ban through the one shared predicate and the one shared read shape, answers a store fault as the door already does, and revokes nothing. The hook choice at the token endpoint is the right seam for the refresh arm (the provider's own user row, before any write). Design holds.

Findings:

- **must-fix (③)** `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` with no filed card — PR body line 3. Edit the three listed surfaces here, or file the rule-level card and write `#N`.
- **must-fix (③)** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts:1-3` — no `// test-budget: SECONDS — spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture: REASON` line on a file over the 10 s line.
- **should** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts:22-27,56-59`, PR body "Token endpoint", changeset line 8 — on the `authorization_code` arm the provider consumes the code and requires the code's session before this hook runs, so for a ban placed through the ban routes the refusal is the provider's own session answer, not this one, and the code is spent; say so, and add a real-provider leg for the code arm beside the refresh leg (`auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts:423-481`).
- **should** PR body "What changes" / changeset — state exactly which doors the rule holds at, naming the authorization server's own endpoints (`auth-route-ledger.ts:352,421,424,428`) either way. Rule level only here; the detail stays with the security seat.
- **question** `packages/runtime/src/security/oauth-subject-ban.ts:50` — a door with no data engine answers "not banned"; documented and identical to today's answer, accepted as is. Confirm it is intended that this stays silent rather than loud.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-r5`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgVfjk2i8T2D4RmxsKg`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `942ee6846660205ce270eb192ce574bf78609619`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/action-confirm-one-dialog.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs (the test-budget grammar), the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.12` (token, userinfo and introspection handlers, subject-identifier resolution) and `better-auth@1.7.12` (the after-hook runner and router error path), read from the pnpm store. The prose faces (`.changeset`, `content/docs/**`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; they are read here sentence by sentence for ② and ③ because the delta's purpose was to land them.

This is a DELTA record by the reviewer of the `949fd3f1e4` record (comment 6663770415): commits `d3daa06af0`, `11504e470d`, `942ee68466` on top of that head. It judges every finding of that record as resolved or not, and reviews the code those commits add in full. `packages/runtime` is unchanged since `949fd3f1e4`; its judgments stand.

### ① Derived judgments

**Findings of the `949fd3f1e4` record:**

- must-fix, `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` with no card — RESOLVED. The line now reads `Skills-docs: updated here`, and the three surfaces are edited in this PR: `administrator-guide.mdx:84-85,184`, `authentication.mdx:1256`, `sys-user.object.ts:210` (the confirmation) and `:219` (the AI description), with the `en` bundle regenerated and the three translated-locale values hand-edited (`check:i18n` sits in Lint & Repo Gates, green). Sentence check below under ③.
- must-fix, no `// test-budget:` header on the dogfood file — RESOLVED. `oauth-banned-subject.dogfood.test.ts:2` declares `// test-budget: 20 — spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture: …; 13.13 s of tests, the slower of two local runs on a shared agent box, x 1.25, rounded up, no CI reading yet, re-measure on CI`. Against the grammar (`measure-test-shard-timings.mjs:1248-1300`): line 2 is inside the header, SECONDS = 20 is a whole multiple of 10 above the 10 s line, CLASS is the exact first class string, REASON is non-empty; 13.13 × 1.25 = 16.4 rounds up to 20. Correct.
- should, the `authorization_code` arm overstated — RESOLVED. `oauth-grant-ban-refusal.ts:20-41,55-61,69-73` now records what each grant has already done when the callback runs (refresh: nothing written; code: consumed, and the code's session required, so a ban placed through the ban routes is answered by the provider's own session check and the callback answers only a code whose session survived; the code is spent either way). PR body "Token endpoint" and changeset line 8 say the same. Two real-provider legs were added (`auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts:498-547`): sessions ended → `400 invalid_request` / `session no longer exists`, no refresh family, and after the unban the same code equals a code never issued (spent); session survived → equals the unknown-code control (`400 invalid_grant` / `invalid code`), no refresh family. Both match the installed provider's handler order as read. Correct.
- should, the authorization server's own doors not named — RESOLVED, by covering them. Body, changeset and docs now list exactly the doors the rule holds at: MCP door, token endpoint (refresh and code), userinfo, introspection. The new code is reviewed below.
- question, a door with no data engine answers "not banned" (`oauth-subject-ban.ts:50`) — not answered in the body or `open_questions`; accepted as is in the prior record and still non-blocking. Carried as a note for the seat.

**New code, in full:**

1. **Userinfo** (`oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.ts:75-83`, wired first in `customUserInfoClaims`, `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:712-722`) — COVERED. In the installed provider the userinfo handler verifies the token, reads the user row and hands it to the operator callback before answering; nothing is written there. The refusal throws the provider's own invalid-access-token error: `401`, body `{ error_description: 'Invalid access token', error: 'invalid_token' }`, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Invalid access token"` — the description and challenge match the provider's constants as read (`INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN_ERROR_DESCRIPTION`, `INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN_WWW_AUTHENTICATE` in the introspect chunk). Envelope equality to a made-up token's answer is pinned on the real provider with AuthManager's own options (`auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts:566-594`: status, body, cache-control, www-authenticate `toEqual`), with the lapse-and-read-again leg and a not-banned control. Judged before the locale claim, so a refused request reads no locale. The row is the provider's read: no added read. The callback receives the real user row, so this door does not depend on the subject-identifier mode. Correct.
2. **Introspection** (`oauth-token-read-ban-refusal.ts:94-108`, a section of AuthManager's global after-hook, `auth-manager-after-hook.ts:142-146`) — COVERED. The JWT introspection path in the installed provider reads no user row and calls no operator callback, so the ban is judged on the produced answer: path `/oauth2/introspect`, an object answer with `active === true` and a non-empty string `sub`, one `internalAdapter.findUserById(sub)`, and on a holding ban the answer is emptied in place and set to `{ active: false }` — the answer a made-up, expired or revoked token gets (RFC 7662 §2.2). In-place mutation is the right shape: better-auth sends `ctx.context.returned` after the hooks when a hook returns nothing (`dispatch.mjs:runAfterHooks`). The real-provider leg (`:596-692`, confidential client, access and refresh tokens, `toEqual` the made-up-token control including cache-control; active again once the ban lapses; not-banned control) proves the rewrite reaches the wire, and the unit leg `:131-141` proves AuthManager's `globalAfterHook` reaches the section through the four sections ahead of it. An inactive answer, a subject-less answer, another path, a non-object answer and an APIError answer read nothing (`:96-113`). Correct.

In the installed after-hook runner a non-APIError thrown from `hooks.after` is re-thrown, so the provider's active answer is never sent: the "never invent" invariant holds, and the request fails.
